author: hoeschec
text:
I have been spending a lot of time trying to understand the concept behind Salivan's deep retrace. It is confusing and complicated, but I think I might be starting to understand it. Here is a chart that I found that seems to illustrate this concept. I apologize for the messy labels...they are all important in explaining the PA. I will do my best to explain (in words) what his happening in the chart. Hopefully Salivan will tell me if I am still wrong...as always, I don't want to mislead anyone here

The deep retrace happens in a PAZ - between two FTR's which form the upper and lower limits of the PAZ. These FTR's also include FL's which act as the origin of the move down and the origin of the move up.

If you look at the chart, you will see the origin of the move down (also target for longs). Price falls from this level, and bounces briefly before faking out (labeled fakeout # 1) below the low of the swap zone confirmation FL Box (red rectangle) where new order flow was created. We identify the decision to fakeout, and wait for price to engulf this DP and form a FTR/FL. This FL/FTR is also the origin of the move up, and will be the target of future shorts (this is very important to remember).

Now that the origin of the move up/target for shorts is formed, we have a completed PAZ (the space between both of the origins). I labeled that in yellow.

Price continues up to the origin of the move down (like Salivan says, these origins act as magnets attracting price). When price reaches this origin, it creates another fakeout to the upside (labeled fakeout # 2). Wait for price to come back down and engulf to the downside (the engulf on the chart is labeled & occurs below the blue rectangle FL Box. This engulf is important because we know the target for that engulf is the origin of the move up (it has not been hit yet, so price will be attracted to it).

Price begins to fall towards the origin of the move up/ target for shorts but does not make it before reversing back to fakeout #2. Price is reversing to gather the remaining OF before continuing on to hit the target. This is good for us, because we will have a very tight stop loss and a wide target (as usual, we zoom in to find the DP to FO, and wait for an engulf of the DP to FO. The FTR/FL that forms after the EG is the best place to wait for an entry. In this case, the short was about 1:13 RR.

I don't know if I am 100% correct but hopefully someone will correct me if I am wrong. The hard part will be finding these live.... but with practice it will be possible.

Incredible potential for building a trading account with a R:R like this.
